Pick the version that matches your audience, and keep the claims honest (see [[Outbound messaging]]).

<span id="answers-to-fair-questions"></span>
== Answers to fair questions ==

'''Is this legal?''' Clean-room reimplementation is a long-established way to build compatible software: you work only from public information and independently write your own code. Interoperating with an API is not the same as copying a product. Each project publishes its clean-room policy and provenance. This is not legal advice.

'''Are you affiliated with Auth0, Okta or Salesforce?''' No. We are independent, and product names are used only to describe compatibility.

'''Can former employees of those companies contribute?''' Yes, but never with confidential knowledge from a former employer. See [[Rules of the road]].

'''Why use AI to build it?''' The incumbents had thousands of engineers and we have a movement. AI agents turn a precise spec into working code quickly. Humans write the specs, review every change and own the result, and compatibility tests against real SDKs decide what counts as done.

'''Is it production-ready?''' Not yet. ZeroAuthy’s first release candidate is an early preview, and its compatibility matrix lists the gaps. SalesCompel is earlier still.

'''What does it cost?''' Nothing. Every project is Apache-2.0: run it, fork it, sell services around it, and contribute back what you can.

'''Why Go, and not Rust?''' Go produces a single self-contained binary that is easy to self-host. Rust recreations are welcome; the specs and compatibility tests are language-neutral. To start one, open an issue naming the project.
